target: uncommitted gpufe/contact.py (gap_normal, sliding_fn, pair_forces) and gpufe/newton.py:100-114 (contact tangent), state of 2026-10-28 ~01:15 (diff + sha256 in work/agents/redteam/r0003_snap/)
claim: The new contact force and its Newton tangent no longer match for frictional contact, which is the path used for the cage. (1) The residual now uses gap_normal() (direction q - ps, smooth fade to zero force when cos(q - ps, facet normal) < 0.5), but the friction-branch tangent (newton.py, 'else' branch) still decides which nodes are active with the old facet-normal gap g = (q - x_s) . n_facet and band 0.05. Nodes in the fade zone (beside an edge) get stiffness for a force they do not have, and the reverse. (2) For mu > 0 the tangent is k I for every active node, stick or slip. For slipping nodes the true tangential stiffness is near zero (force magnitude fixed at mu p), so Newton over-stiffens them. With the strict line search, any increment with many slipping nodes is likely to be halved repeatedly, or to stop the run ('Newton not converged after cuts'). The run stops rather than giving a wrong number, so this is minor. But it means the frictional checks may simply not finish on the designs that slip most. The exact autodiff tangent was added only for mu = 0. (3) The fade sets the contact force to zero for a slave node whose closest master point lies on a boundary edge at a shallow angle. A cage node that slides past the rim of the meshed endplate surface (or of an endplate region missing from the master surface) therefore meets no resistance. A designer could exploit this at the endplate rim if footprints reach it (inset is 1 mm). Not tested, unverified as an exploit.
evidence: work/agents/redteam/r0003_snap/gpufe_diff_*.patch and gpufe_sha_*.txt; gpufe/contact.py gap_normal (c0 0.2, c1 0.5, 'gets no force'); gpufe/newton.py lines ~107-112: 'g = ((q - x[p.s]) * nrm).sum(-1); act = ((g > -contact_band) & (d < p.R)); M = eye(3) if p.mu > 0'. No gate exercises this path (F-0023).
how_to_reproduce: git diff gpufe/ (or the saved patch); read sliding_fn vs the 'else' branch of NewtonSolver._entries. Suggested test: gate 1c on Newton (block dragged to gross slip) and count increment cuts / iterations with the current tangent vs an autodiff tangent of sliding_fn.

fix_options.option: Use the same autodiff (jvp) tangent for the frictional pair force (stick: anchor-based; slip: return-mapped) as for mu = 0, so residual and tangent come from one function.
At least use gap_normal for the active set and a slip-consistent tangential stiffness for slipping nodes.
Add to the gates: a slave node sliding off the master edge must not lose contact force without a geometric reason.

summary_zh: 求解器正在修改中、尚未提交的接觸程式有一個不一致：計算接觸力和計算收斂方向（牛頓法的切線矩陣）用的是兩套不同的規則。有摩擦的情況正是 cage 要用的情況。對於正在滑動的節點，切線矩陣把它們當成黏住、非常硬，所以牛頓法會一直縮小步長，甚至讓計算中止。這不會產生錯誤的數字，但最容易滑動的設計可能根本算不完。另外，新規則讓滑過端板表面邊緣的節點完全沒有接觸力，設計者可能利用這點（尚未測試）。建議：有摩擦時也用自動微分算切線矩陣，讓兩者出自同一個函數，並加入對應的驗證關卡。
